svg.title: MVCC
svg.desc: MVCC. Multi-version concurrency control: an update writes a new row version, readers see a snapshot, and vacuum removes dead versions. Step 1, Locks: readers vs writers: A report that locks the orders it reads makes the cancel of order 495179 wait 5 s, then fail. Step 2, Row versions & snapshots: UPDATE writes a new version and sets xmax on the old one; the report's snapshot still sees the old. Step 3, VACUUM and the horizon: While the report stays open, VACUUM removes none of 3,001 dead versions; after COMMIT, all of them. Step 4, Costs and other engines: Old versions cost bloat, vacuuming and XID freezing; InnoDB and Oracle keep them in undo instead.

g.text: A report that locks the orders it reads makes the cancel of order 495179 wait 5 s, then fail.
UPDATE writes a new version and sets xmax on the old one; the report's snapshot still sees the old.
While the report stays open, VACUUM removes none of 3,001 dead versions; after COMMIT, all of them.
Old versions cost bloat, vacuuming and XID freezing; InnoDB and Oracle keep them in undo instead.
lock-based: the report locks the table it reads
MVCC: the report reads its snapshot, the writer never waits
the report stays open while 3,000 more orders change
the same report and writer: old versions wait in undo logs
